title: What Are Your Fundamental Rights?
summary: Six rights the Constitution gives every person in India, and what they actually mean in daily life.

body.text: The Constitution of India gives every person some basic rights that no one - not the police, not your employer, not the government - can simply take away. These are called Fundamental Rights.

items: Right to Equality (Articles 14-18): equal treatment before the law.
Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22): speech, movement, and protection during arrest.
Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24): no forced labour and no child labour.
Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32): go to court when a right is violated.

body.text: Article 21, the right to life and personal liberty, has been read by the Supreme Court to include dignity, privacy, health and a clean environment.
How these rights protect you day to day

If a shop refuses you service only because of your religion or caste, that is an equality issue. If the police detain you without telling you why, that is a freedom issue. If your employer holds back your wages for months, courts have linked fair wages to the right to life.
Rights come with limits. Freedom of speech does not protect threats, hate speech or defamation.
If a government action violates a Fundamental Right, Article 32 lets you approach the Supreme Court directly, or Article 226 a High Court.

practicalSteps: Write down what happened, with dates, places and names.
Keep copies of any documents, messages or receipts.
Ask for the reason in writing whenever a right is restricted.
For free help, contact your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call the NALSA helpline 15100.
exceptions: Some rights can be restricted during a declared emergency (Articles 352-360), but Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.
Reasonable restrictions are allowed in the public interest, such as for public order or decency.

faqs.q: Can a private company violate my Fundamental Rights?
faqs.a: Fundamental Rights mainly apply against the State. Against private parties you usually rely on ordinary laws such as contract, labour and consumer law. A few rights, like Articles 15(2), 17, 23 and 24, do apply to private persons.

faqs.q: Is free legal aid really free?
faqs.a: Yes, for people who qualify by income and category. Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, every district has a Legal Services Authority.

misconceptions.myth: Fundamental Rights are only for citizens.
misconceptions.fact: Most apply to every person in India. A few, such as Articles 15, 16, 19 and 29, apply only to citizens.
